description: Cross-continental epidemiological surveillance of artisanal mining (ASM) respiratory morbidity in the DRC, calibrated via Jamaican bauxite surveillance using Sentinel-1 SAR, MODIS MAIAC AOD, ERA5 meteorology, GLiM crystalline-silica priors, RMT-CORAL + DANN transfer learning, and R SIR/DiD models.
summary:
We developed a cross-continental environmental epidemiology and transfer-learning surveillance pipeline that detects and quantifies underreported respiratory morbidity (such as acute respiratory illness and silicosis) across artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) corridors in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC_Kolwezi, DRC_Ituri_Mongbwalu), calibrated against validated public health surveillance from Jamaican bauxite-mining parishes (JM_St_Ann, JM_Manchester, JM_Portland_Ctrl).

To overcome missing ground air monitors and clinic reporting blind spots in remote mining zones, the pipeline fuses boundary-layer-normalized MODIS MAIAC aerosol optical depth (MCD19A2), all-weather Sentinel-1 C-band radar (RTC), ERA5 meteorology, and Global Lithological Map (GLiM v1.0) crystalline-silica toxicity priors. A Random Matrix Theory covariance-aligned Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (RMT-CORAL + DANN) transfers dose-response relationships from Jamaica to the DRC, followed by Exact Poisson Standardized Incidence Ratio (SIR), Negative Binomial, and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) validation in R.

This framework is critical because artisanal miners face severe crystalline-silica exposure yet remain largely invisible in national health statistics. By turning open satellite data into actionable respiratory surveillance alerts, health ministries and NGOs can deploy targeted screening clinics, protective gear, and dust-mitigation interventions where underreporting gaps are widest.
details: What Does It Do & How Does It Work?This project is a cross-continental environmental epidemiology and transfer-learning surveillance pipeline that detects and quantifies underreported respiratory morbidity (such as acute respiratory illness and silicosis) in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) corridors of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC_Kolwezi and DRC_Ituri_Mongbwalu), calibrated against validated public health surveillance from Jamaican bauxite-mining parishes (JM_St_Ann, JM_Manchester, and control parish JM_Portland_Ctrl). The pipeline operates across four integrated stages: Multi-Modal Satellite & Atmospheric Exposure Physics: It ingests cloud-masked daily 1 km MODIS MAIAC aerosol optical depth (MCD19A2 v061) normalized by ECMWF ERA5 planetary boundary layer height (BLH) to estimate surface-level particulate concentration, and pairs ERA5 10 m wind advection vectors with all-weather Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band Radiometric Terrain Corrected (RTC) backscatter and Grey-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) surface roughness to detect active excavation dust generation. Feature Screening & Random Matrix Theory (RMT) Alignment: It applies Taguchi orthogonal array signal-to-noise feature screening alongside Ledoit-Péché analytical nonlinear covariance shrinkage (RMT-CORAL) to denoise high-dimensional environmental covariates and align second-order feature statistics across continents. Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) Morbidity Transfer: A 2-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) sequence encoder processes 12-week rolling environmental windows and trains jointly on a masked Huber morbidity regressor (anchored to Jamaica's weekly Ministry of Health & Wellness syndromic surveillance) and a Gradient Reversal Layer (GRL) domain discriminator to project expected respiratory incidence into DRC mining zones without requiring labeled DRC clinical training data.   Lithological Silica Weighting & Statistical Triangulation (R): Predicted exposure is weighted by crystalline-silica toxicity priors derived from the Global Lithological Map (GLiM v1.0)—yielding silica multipliers of 1.596 for DRC_Kolwezi and 1.750 for DRC_Ituri_Mongbwalu—and validated in R using Exact Poisson Standardized Incidence Ratios (SIR), Negative Binomial count regression, and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) dust-spike slope attenuation models. What Benefits Does It Have? Solves the Clinical Surveillance Blind Spot: Remote ASM corridors frequently lack consistent clinic reporting, diagnostic imaging, or ground-based air quality monitors. By transferring calibrated dose-response curves from a data-rich mining region (Jamaica) to an under-monitored region (DRC), the system estimates true respiratory disease burden using freely available global satellite and reanalysis feeds.   All-Weather & Physics-Grounded Monitoring: Combining C-band Sentinel-1 radar (which penetrates tropical cloud cover) with ERA5 boundary-layer scaling avoids the optical cloud-gap failures and column-versus-surface biases common in standard AOD-only air quality models. Mineral-Specific Toxicity Differentiation: Rather than treating all particulate matter as equally toxic, integrating GLiM v1.0 lithology distinguishes lower-silica bauxite/laterite dust from high-crystalline-silica quartz/granitoid tailings that drive irreversible silicosis and tuberculosis susceptibility. Open, Reproducible Architecture: Packaged with standardized directory layouts, MIT licensing, CITATION.cff metadata, and automated R diagnostic plots (SIR forest plots, DiD slope attenuation curves, and DANN vs. observed time-series charts), public health teams can rerun or adapt the pipeline to new mining districts.   What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?Targeted Public Health Resource Allocation: Equip ministries of health, NGOs, and district health teams (such as DHIS2 health-zone administrators in Kolwezi and Ituri) with early-warning surveillance alerts to deploy mobile respiratory screening clinics, N95/P100 respiratory protection, and tuberculosis/silicosis diagnostics where underreporting gaps are widest.​ Environmental & Occupational Policy Enforcement: Provide quantitative epidemiological evidence linking localized excavation spikes and downwind dust advection to acute respiratory surges, supporting wet-drilling mandates, tailings stabilization, and buffer-zone protections for nearby communities.Scalable Global Blueprint: Establish a transferable framework adaptable to other under-monitored artisanal gold, cobalt, copper, and stone-quarrying regions across Sub-Saharan Africa, South America, and Southeast Asia.What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Did You Use?​ Coding Languages: Python 3.11 (satellite extraction, signal processing, RMT covariance alignment, PyTorch deep learning) and R 4.3 (biostatistical validation and publication graphics).Python Scientific & Deep Learning Stack: PyTorch (2-layer GRU + DANN Gradient Reversal Layer), NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, scikit-image (GLCM texture features), GeoPandas, rioxarray, xarray, netCDF4, Matplotlib, and Seaborn.​ Earth Observation & Cloud APIs: earthaccess (NASA EOSDIS LP DAAC for MODIS MCD19A2 v061), asf_search and hyp3_sdk (Alaska Satellite Facility HyP3 cloud-native Sentinel-1 RTC processing), and cdsapi (Copernicus Climate Data Store for ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis).   R Statistical & Visualization Stack: dplyr, tidyr, MASS (Negative Binomial regression), pscl (zero-inflated count modeling), sandwich & lmtest (robust standard errors for DiD), stats::poisson.test (Exact Poisson SIR), and ggplot2.Geospatial Data & Version Control: Global Lithological Map (GLiM v1.0 GeoPackage), Conda environment management, Git, and GitHub. Hardware: Developed and executed locally on an Apple Silicon MacBook Pro (12-thread CPU execution for PyTorch DANN training, spatial raster processing, and R statistical modeling), off-loading heavy SAR radiometric terrain correction to ASF's cloud HyP3 infrastructure. How Is Your Project Creative?Cross-Continental Epidemiological Transfer Learning: Instead of waiting years for ground air monitors or complete clinical registries in remote DRC mining towns, the project bridges two continents—pairing Jamaican bauxite parish surveillance (W-MON) with DRC artisanal cobalt/gold corridors via domain-adversarial deep learning.Fusing Quantum/Random Matrix Theory with Environmental Health: Applying Ledoit-Péché analytical nonlinear covariance shrinkage from Random Matrix Theory (RMT-CORAL) and industrial Taguchi orthogonal array screening prevents small-sample noise from corrupting cross-continental neural feature alignment.​ Lithology-Informed Toxicity Priors (GLiM): Bridging structural geology and clinical epidemiology by weighting satellite-observed particulate plumes with bedrock free-crystalline-silica fractions (1.596x–1.750x toxicity multipliers) directly addresses the pathological difference between nuisance dust and fibrogenic silica.​ Difference-in-Differences (DiD) Underreporting Detection: Using dust-spike slope attenuation in R as a statistical fingerprint to distinguish genuine low disease incidence from overwhelmed or under-capturing local clinics turns routine count data into an actionable surveillance-gap detector.​ What Factors Did Your Team Consider?Atmospheric Physics vs. Column AOD Bias: Satellite AOD measures the entire vertical atmospheric column, whereas humans breathe surface air; normalizing MODIS AOD by ERA5 Planetary Boundary Layer Height (BLH) accounts for seasonal inversion trapping and dilution. Cloud Cover & Seasonal Meteorology: Tropical regions like Jamaica and the Congo Basin experience persistent cloud cover and distinct wet/dry seasons; integrating all-weather Sentinel-1 C-band radar and ERA5 wind/precipitation controls prevents seasonal observation bias. Mineralogical Toxicity Differences: Bauxite dust in Jamaica and quartz-rich gold/copper-cobalt host rock in the DRC carry different fibrogenic risks, motivating the explicit GLiM v1.0 crystalline-silica scaling layer. Overdispersion, Zero-Inflation, and Surveillance Capture Bias: Weekly clinic respiratory counts exhibit high variance and reporting gaps; pairing Exact Poisson SIR with Negative Binomial regression and DiD spike-attenuation tests ensures statistical robustness. Data Privacy, Governance & Transparency: All epidemiological analyses are aggregated at the parish or administrative health-zone level with zero personally identifiable patient data, API credentials (~/.netrc, ~/.cdsapirc) are strictly isolated from version control, and DRC clinic capture figures are explicitly documented as DANN-anchored simulations pending empirical district-level DHIS2 integration.
